name: Peter Murphy
label: Beggars Banquet
lede: The voice of Bauhaus spent his first solo years learning to make records without a band behind him, then landed a seven-week number one on American modern rock radio and moved to Istanbul.

eras.title: The printer's boy who sang over the machines
eras.text: Murphy grew up Catholic in Wellingborough, the seventh of nine children, and left school for a printing job. His schoolfriend Daniel Ash heard him and pulled him into Bauhaus, where Murphy wrote words and the others wrote the music. That arrangement ended in 1983, and so did the band.

years.h: Peter Murphy is born in Northampton
years.p: Seventh of nine children in a working-class family of Irish descent, raised in Wellingborough. He credits the choral hymns of school Mass as an early influence.

years.cap: Murphy with Bauhaus at Tuts, Chicago
years.h: Daniel Ash asks him to join a band, and Bauhaus begins
years.p: Murphy, Ash, David J and Kevin Haskins form [[Bauhaus|0688add2-c282-4ee2-ba61-223ffdb3c201]] in Northampton. Murphy had found his voice singing albums at full volume over the printing-shop machines.
years.xp:
"To drown it out, I'd sing albums, back to back, at full volume," he told FLOOD in 2025. "That's when I realized I actually had a voice."

Ash remembered the first rehearsal for Murphy's biographer Ian Shirley: Murphy just started singing from the newspaper, and Ash knew within five minutes.

years.h: Bowie and Deneuve's vampire film opens on Murphy
years.p: Bauhaus play 'Bela Lugosi's Dead' over the opening of The Hunger, and the camera barely leaves the singer. The band split the same year.
years.xp: Murphy's face also ended up in comics: Neil Gaiman has said Murphy was the original model for Dream in The Sandman, and James O'Barr based Eric in The Crow heavily on him.

eras.title: Learning to make a record alone
eras.text: Without Ash, David J and Haskins writing the music, Murphy had no idea how to start. He tried dance, turned down film roles, made one album with Mick Karn of Japan, and finally built a solo record with a collaborator who had never heard Bauhaus.

years.h: Murphy turns down Fletcher Christian
years.p: He was offered the part in the Bounty remake and auditioned for Tarzan in Greystoke. Self-conscious about a slight stammer, he passed on most of it, and on a solo deal from Beggars Banquet.
years.xp: Derek Jarman wanted him for Caravaggio. Murphy also refused a follow-up Maxell ad because, he said, "they wanted me to go through space with this dolly bird." A televised dance in a sandpit to Bauhaus's 'Hollow Hills' went badly; Murphy admitted "it looked rather silly really."

years.h: Dalis Car makes one album and stops
years.p: Murphy and [[Mick Karn|0cc52b63-c9bc-4130-81d3-1ca0c31804a7]] of [[Japan|697e7111-5630-4c77-83f3-39821bacc61a]] meet through a Japanese journalist who'd interviewed both. The name came from a friend's dream about buying Salvador Dalí's car, not from Captain Beefheart.
years.xp:
Karn left gaps for vocals; Murphy wanted to leave the musical breaks alone. Drummer Paul Vincent Lawson's nerves meant he ended up programming most of the patterns. On The Old Grey Whistle Test one commentator said they looked like investment bankers after a bad day on the market.

The album went over budget and didn't sell. Karn wanted to continue; Murphy stayed in Turkey with his wife rather than come in for the single's bonus tracks.

years.h: Howard Hughes admits he's never heard Bauhaus
years.p: Murphy takes the train to Cornwall to meet the Associates' Hughes, and jokingly demands to be driven back to the station. Their demos win a Beggars Banquet deal; 'Final Solution', a Pere Ubu cover, reaches 92.
years.xp: Murphy picked [[Ivo Watts-Russell|cf86cec1-1baf-4d8a-ba1e-01568332585a]] of 4AD to produce, though Watts-Russell had never produced an album, because he liked his mixing on It'll End in Tears. Murphy and Hughes later remixed most of it themselves; Watts-Russell's 'Final Solution' stayed.

years.h: 'The Answer Is Clear' answers Daniel Ash
years.p: Murphy heard Ash's [[Tones on Tail|ff3a293a-76d1-49a7-a5c5-fede02e7e648]] song 'Movement of Fear' as being about him, and wrote back on Should the World Fail to Fall Apart. The album reached 82 in the UK.
years.xp: Venezuelan painter Carlos Sosa, a friend, did the cover: Murphy talked Beggars into flying him over and they painted it together in Murphy's attic. John McGeoch recreated his own guitar part for a cover of Magazine's 'The Light Pours Out of Me'.

eras.title: Cuts You Up, and RCA caught off guard
eras.text: Keyboardist Paul Statham became Murphy's writing partner and the touring band became the Hundred Men. Beggars licensed him to RCA in America, where college radio took to him and, in 1990, a single sold faster than the label could keep up with.

years.h: Hughes picks his own band over the American tour
years.p: Howard Hughes leaves for the Western Approaches, and Paul Statham of B-Movie takes over keyboards and writing. The 19-date North American run starts in Boston on February 10.

years.h: Simon Rogers gets the job over Eno and Lanois
years.p: Love Hysteria mixes in samples of Japanese fishermen and Jean Cocteau. 'All Night Long' lands on MTV, and RCA gives Murphy his first proper US release.
years.xp: Statham wrote backing tracks locked in Murphy's attic in Primrose Hill on a four-track. The tour with [[The Church|4fcb7864-42dd-4dcf-b269-6da0d9042956]] in America included a cover of Prince's 'Purple Rain', and the backing band took the name the Hundred Men.

years.h: Platinum blond, and back to a harder sound
years.p: Deep sells about 350,000 copies in America, according to Ian Shirley's biography, and reaches the Billboard 200's forties.

years.h: 'Cuts You Up' holds number one on modern rock radio for seven weeks
years.p: The string line started as a sample. A session viola player played it beautifully, Rogers said, and it still sounded worse than the sample.
years.xp:
Statham said the single sold 250,000 copies in three weeks and RCA were caught on the hop: a cardboard Murphy in the forecourt of Tower Records in Los Angeles, and twenty or thirty label people backstage every night, "like Spinal Tap."

At the Fender Ballroom in Los Angeles, with [[Jane's Addiction|e3434cc7-d348-491a-9dc8-325af3d9086d]] opening, guitarist Pete Bonas remembered people passing out at the front and oxygen bottles on stage. Shirley also reports a 25,000 crowd at the Universal Amphitheatre.

eras.title: A cassock on late-night TV, then Istanbul
eras.text: Holy Smoke arrived as grunge took over, and RCA's team had changed. Murphy moved his family to Istanbul, dissolved the Hundred Men and made one more Beggars record with Statham before both moved on.

years.h: Anton Corbijn shoots a cover Murphy calls a statement against image
years.p: Producer Mike Thorne came at Martin Mills's suggestion. Holy Smoke sold about 100,000 copies in America, well short of Deep.
years.xp: Murphy lined the Corbijn proofs up in his house for a week before choosing the one that haunted him. Paul Morley wrote the press release, mostly about the shape of Murphy's head.

q: I turned up in a cassock!
years.h: Murphy's first big American TV spot, in a cassock
years.p: He sings 'You're So Close' on The Dennis Miller Show. Looking back, he said he came across to the mass audience as some weird, theatrical English bloke.

years.h: Murphy moves to Istanbul and ends the Hundred Men
years.p: His wife, Beyhan Foulkes, is head choreographer of the Turkish National Modern Dance group. Murphy, raised Catholic, later converted to Sufism.
years.xp: At the end of the Holy Smoke tour Murphy said the band had run its course. Shirley notes the Hundred Men had no contract with Beggars or RCA and had been paid weekly by Murphy's management for seven years.

years.h: Cascade closes out the Beggars years
years.p: Ambient pop with Pascal Gabriel producing and Michael Brook's infinite guitar. Statham leaves to form Peach and later writes for Dido and Kylie Minogue.
years.xp: Programming started at Peter Gabriel's Real World Studios near Bath, then moved to Spain for six weeks. Murphy played 'The Scarlet Thing in You' on The Jon Stewart Show on May 23, 1995, and Jewel opened his North American tour.

eras.title: Bauhaus again, and Turkey in the music
eras.text: After Beggars, Murphy hopped labels, reformed Bauhaus twice and made his most Turkish record with Mercan Dede. By 2008 he was working with Trent Reznor.

years.h: KMFDM rework the old songs for Red Ant
years.p: The Recall EP pairs Murphy with Sascha Konietzko, Bill Rieflin and Tim Skold. Red Ant also had [[Love and Rockets|8cb3aa4a-3b4c-48b8-be0a-e57010fc1430]], which set off Bauhaus reunion rumours before the label folded.

years.h: Bauhaus reform for the Resurrection tour
years.p: A night at New York's Hammerstein Ballroom becomes the Gotham DVD on Metropolis Records.

years.h: Just violin, guitar and that voice at the El Rey
years.p: Hugh Marsh on electric violin and Peter DiStefano of Porno for Pyros on guitar; the Los Angeles set becomes aLive Just for Love. That year he also surprises Seattle's Convergence goth festival with an acoustic set.

years.cap: Houston, May 30, 2002, on the Dust tour
years.h: Dust, made with Mercan Dede, is the one he's proudest of
years.p: Traditional Turkish instruments and Dede's electronics, on Metropolis. Fans hoping for something uptempo were put off; Murphy calls it his most unusual work and singles out 'Your Face'.

years.h: Bauhaus are back, and this time they make an album
years.p: The 2005 reunion runs to a 2007 tour with [[Nine Inch Nails|b7ffd2af-418f-4be2-bdd1-22f8b48613da]] and Go Away White in 2008, released just before they split again.

yt: 'Warm Leatherette' with Trent Reznor and Jeordie White
years.h: Trent Reznor brings him in for 'Warm Leatherette'
years.p: Murphy, [[Trent Reznor|bc880664-6751-4998-984d-ebdbff15d229]] and Jeordie White cover the Normal in a small studio session posted by Nine Inch Nails. In 2009 Murphy guests with NIN at Terminal 5 and Chicago's Aragon Ballroom.

eras.title: Vampires, Dalis Car and 35 years of Bauhaus
eras.text: Murphy played a vampire for Twilight, finished Dalis Car with a dying Mick Karn, and toured 35 years of Bauhaus songs. The decade also brought a drug arrest in California and a heart attack during a New York residency.

years.h: He plays 'The Cold One' in Twilight: Eclipse
years.p: A cameo in The Twilight Saga: Eclipse. That summer he starts the Dirty Dirt Tour ahead of Ninth (2011).

years.h: Murphy and Karn reunite for four Dalis Car songs
years.p: They hadn't seen each other since 1983, and Karn had stage-four cancer. He died on January 4, 2011; the songs came out as the InGladAloneness EP in 2012.

years.src: Rolling Stone: Bauhaus' Peter Murphy Arrested · Consequence
years.h: A witness chases Murphy from Glendale to Los Angeles and blocks his car
years.p: He was arrested over a rear-end crash on suspicion of DUI causing injury, felony hit-and-run and methamphetamine possession. In October he pleaded guilty to the meth charge and got three years' probation.
years.xp:
Rolling Stone reported that Murphy, who appeared "very confused", denied drinking and said he'd taken prescription medication and was jet-lagged; police said they found a small bag of possible methamphetamine. Bail was set at $500,000.

Per Consequence, he pleaded no contest to misdemeanor hit-and-run and guilty to possession, with 45 days of Narcotics Anonymous meetings, 10 days of community service and random drug tests.

years.h: The Mr Moonlight Tour sings 35 years of Bauhaus
years.p: With guitarist Mark Thwaite, drummer Nick Lucero and bassist Emilio DiZefalo-China, the tour runs through Europe, the US, China, Russia, Australia and New Zealand.

years.h: Lion, produced by Youth
years.p: The [[Killing Joke|f5aca88c-e3c1-4bc2-af33-68a9a9f7b56a]] bassist produces, and the album reaches 173 on the Billboard 200.

years.cap: Murphy at The Chapel, San Francisco, March 2019
years.src: Wikipedia: Peter Murphy · Rolling Stone: Peter Murphy Enters Rehab
years.h: A heart attack on night eight of a New York residency
years.p: Murphy was taken from (Le) Poisson Rouge to Lenox Hill Hospital for angioplasty and two stents. Ten days later he announced a full recovery; the dates were made up in January 2020.
years.xp: Later that year Bauhaus played three reunion shows in Los Angeles, the start of a run that lasted into 2022.

eras.title: Rehab, then Silver Shade
eras.text: Bauhaus's last run ended early when Murphy went into rehab. Three years later he came back with his first solo album in eleven years, recorded with Youth and guests from Nine Inch Nails, Tool and Culture Club.

years.src: Rolling Stone: Peter Murphy Enters Rehab
years.h: Bauhaus cancel their autumn US tour as Murphy enters rehab
years.p: The band's statement said he was going into a rehabilitation facility "to attend to his health and well-being." Earlier that year they had released their first new song in 14 years, written by the exquisite corpse method.

q: I am a singer who makes music.
years.h: Boy George, Trent Reznor and Tool's bassist turn up on Silver Shade
years.p: Youth produces again, for Metropolis. 'Let the Flowers Grow' is a duet with Boy George; Reznor sings on 'Swoon'; Justin Chancellor of [[Tool|66fc5bf8-daa4-4241-b378-9bc9077939d2]] plays too.
